SIP uses UDP or TCP on 5060 and TLS on 5061, and a request that does not fit one datagram needs a connection.

text: The first INVITE has a magic-cookie branch, Max-Forwards 70, a From tag, and no To tag.
A trace shows a user agent, a proxy, a registrar, a redirect server, or a B2BUA, and products often combine those roles.
roomTitle: Roles a trace is actually showing

text: The core methods are INVITE, ACK, OPTIONS, BYE, CANCEL, and REGISTER, and status codes fall into six classes.
Compact header names are aliases from RFC 3261, with a few more aliases defined in the extension RFCs.
A transaction is identified by the branch, and a retransmission repeats that branch instead of starting a new one.
A dialog is identified by Call-ID, the From tag, and the To tag, and the initial request has no To tag.
T1 seeds retransmissions, 64 times T1 ends the transaction, and Timer C is the proxy's longer INVITE arm.
roomTitle: T1, the transaction timeout, and Timer C

text: The transport is a property of the hop, written in Via, and it changes retransmission and framing rather than the SIP methods.
The ACK for a non-2xx is hop by hop inside the INVITE transaction, and the ACK for a 2xx is a new end-to-end transaction.
A proxy that wants to stay on the dialog prepends a Record-Route URI, and that URI has to contain lr.
A provisional response with Require: 100rel is retransmitted until PRACK, and RAck names that exact response.
UPDATE can change the session while the initial INVITE is still outstanding, and it does not use the ACK rules.
Session timers name who refreshes the dialog, and 422 tells the caller the interval was below Min-SE.
CANCEL abandons an unanswered INVITE, BYE ends a confirmed dialog, and re-INVITE changes a dialog that already exists.
REFER asks another UA to send a request, and Replaces names the dialog that request should take over.
REGISTER binds an address-of-record to one or more Contacts, and the registrar is a different role from the proxy.
RFC 3263 turns a SIP domain into a transport, a port, and an address with NAPTR, SRV, and A or AAAA.
With lr, the Request-URI stays the remote target, each hop pops its own Route, and Max-Forwards of 0 yields 483.
RFC 5626 binds a UA instance to one or more flows with reg-id and +sip.instance, and keepalives hold those flows open.
Path is the inbound vector stored with a binding, and Service-Route is the outbound vector the registrar gives the UA.
A GRUU routes to one UA instance, and the registrar returns it as pub-gruu or temp-gruu on the binding.
A forking proxy creates one client transaction per binding, and each To tag is a separate early dialog.
Read v, o, s, c, t, m, and a lines as a session description. RFC 8866 is the current SDP specification.
roomTitle: The lines in an SDP body

text: RFC 3264 matches streams by position. The answer has the same number of m-lines, in the same order.
Match codecs by the rtpmap encoding name. The G.722 rtpmap clock stays 8000.
sendrecv, sendonly, recvonly, and inactive are per stream. Hold is commonly sendonly or inactive.
Port 0 refuses the stream in that slot. The m-line stays, with a protocol and a format list.
183 Session Progress with SDP is the usual early-media pattern. 180 means ringing. A 183 does not always have SDP.
RFC 6337 is the usage document for offer/answer mistakes: order, version, delayed offer, and hold.
RTP version 2 carries a sequence number, a timestamp, an SSRC, and a marker bit. SIP does not carry those fields.
RFC 3551 assigns static payload types. Dynamic types are named by rtpmap, and G.722 stays at clock 8000.
Choose a codec both sides named. Read RFC 6716 and the Opus license before you draw any legal conclusion.
RTCP sender reports and receiver reports describe the RTP flow. A SIP 200 OK does not report loss.
telephone-event is RFC 4733, a dynamic payload. Events 0 through 15 are DTMF. INFO and KPML are different tools.
ptime is SDP. Twenty milliseconds of G.711 is 50 packets per second and 160 bytes of payload, plus headers. Voice sits in the EF class.
A 200 OK can be perfect while one RTP direction is missing. Read direction, c=, and who is actually sending.
A 401 from a UAS is answered with Authorization. A 407 from a proxy is answered with Proxy-Authorization.
SIP over TLS is RFC 3261 section 18. The certificate has to identify the SIP domain, per RFC 5922.
SRTP is RFC 3711. SDES a=crypto is RFC 4568. DTLS-SRTP is RFC 5764. An SBC must not assume peers share one method.
Privacy is RFC 3323. P-Asserted-Identity and P-Preferred-Identity are for trusted networks, not cryptographic identity.
STIR is RFC 8224, PASSporT is RFC 8225, certificates are RFC 8226, and the SHAKEN extension is RFC 8588. Attestation levels are ATIS.
Scanning, registration hijack, and toll fraud are classes of abuse. The response is authentication, exposure control, and alerting.
A defensive edge limits peers, requires digest and TLS, strips PAI, and does not share SRTP keying across legs.
SIP and SDP embed IP addresses. NAT rewrites the packet header and leaves those embedded addresses behind.
RFC 3581 adds rport so the response is sent to the source address and port the request came from.
STUN, RFC 8489, lets a client learn the address a server sees. It obsoletes RFC 5389.
TURN, RFC 8656, allocates a relay when host and server-reflexive paths fail. It obsoletes RFC 5766.
ICE is RFC 8445, which obsoletes RFC 5245. Candidates are host, srflx, prflx, and relay.
A SIP ALG rewrites SIP and SDP in transit and often corrupts the call. It cannot rewrite TLS.
Many SBCs learn the remote RTP address from the first packet instead of trusting c=. That is deployment practice, and RFC 5853 is the requirements RFC.
RFC 5853 collects requirements from SBC deployments. It does not define an SBC wire protocol.
roomTitle: RFC 5853 is requirements, not a protocol

An SBC can refuse a new INVITE when its configured budget is exhausted. The number itself is platform-specific.

P-Asserted-Identity is a network-asserted identity. An SBC at a trust boundary decides whether that assertion continues.
The certificate name and the SIP Contact need to be names the peer accepts. Teams and Webex Local Gateway do not share a wildcard rule.
Direct Routing uses the pstnhub proxies on 5061, a certified SBC, and a verified domain. Contact must be an FQDN.
OPTIONS followed by 200 marks the SBC healthy. Media processors use SRTP. The protocol article’s OPTIONS CSeq cell disagrees with RFC 3261.
An IOS XE Local Gateway uses SIP TLS and SRTP. Third-party SBCs use a certificate-based trunk. Wildcard certificates are not supported. ByoPSTN means bring your own PSTN.
